item.title: 🎙 Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s opening remarks during talks with Foreign Minister of the Republic of Abkhazia Oleg Bartsits
item.description: 🎙 Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s opening remarks during talks with Foreign Minister of the Republic of Abkhazia Oleg Bartsits (Moscow, October 1, 2026) 💬 First of all, we would like to congratulate you on Abkhazia's Victory and Independence Day , which you celebrated yesterday. President of Russia Vladimir Putin sent his congratulations on this occasion. We cherish this chapter of our modern history. Turning to our bilateral relations, they are developing dynamically . A key event in 2026 was the meeting between Presidents Vladimir Putin and Badra Gunba in Moscow on May 9. They agreed to expand our bilateral cooperation and identified specific socioeconomic and humanitarian projects. This sets a practical agenda for all of us , with our Ministries playing a coordinating role, as stipulated in our Presidents’ decrees. Today, we will discuss in detail the progress of our joint work on the international stage . We note that major initiatives are being implemented, including the reconstruction of embankment in Sukhum, hot meals in schools and a new hub for the We Are Together NGO . These projects truly reflect the realities of our relations today, the affinity between our peoples and the friendship that binds them. 📈 We see considerable potential for investment cooperation , as demonstrated by the First Abkhazian International Economic Forum . We will continue to develop this area. It is encouraging that bilateral trade grew by 16% in 2025 . This is a very good result.

🎙
Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s
opening remarks
during talks with Foreign Minister of the Republic of Abkhazia Oleg Bartsits
(Moscow, October 1, 2026)
💬
First of all, we would like to congratulate you on
Abkhazia's
Victory and Independence Day
, which you celebrated yesterday. President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
sent his congratulations
on this occasion. We cherish this chapter of our modern history.
Turning to our bilateral relations, they are developing dynamically
. A key event in 2026 was
the meeting
between Presidents
Vladimir Putin
and
Badra Gunba
in Moscow on May 9. They agreed to expand our bilateral cooperation and identified specific socioeconomic and humanitarian projects.
This sets a practical agenda for all of us
, with our Ministries playing a coordinating role, as stipulated in our Presidents’ decrees.
Today, we will discuss in detail the progress of our joint work on the international stage
. We note that major initiatives are being implemented, including the reconstruction of embankment in Sukhum, hot meals in schools and a new hub for
the We Are Together NGO
. These projects truly reflect the realities of our relations today, the affinity between our peoples and the friendship that binds them.
📈
We see considerable potential for investment cooperation
, as demonstrated by
the First Abkhazian International Economic Forum
. We will continue to develop this area. It is encouraging that
bilateral trade grew by 16% in 2025
. This is a very good result.
Abkhazia is a popular destination for Russian tourists
. The number of excursions to your country
has already increased by more than 40% in 2026
. President of Abkhazia
Badra Gunba
has said that he aims to ensure that
the Republic welcomes five million visitors annually by 2030
. We will certainly do everything we can to help achieve this target. Naturally, this will require investment in infrastructure and measures to ensure safety and security.
We will support independent Abkhazia’s development in every area without exception
, including domestic development, external relations and coordination on the international stage.
Speaking of international affairs, I know that you recently visited
the Syrian Arab Republic
. I would be grateful to hear your impressions and plans.
🤝
We will review all the issues on our agenda and later with our colleague from South Ossetia
Akhsar Dzhioev
discuss
current international issues and regional security
, including
the International Discussions on Security and Stability in the South Caucasus
. This format requires our constant attention. I therefore believe that our meeting today is very timely.

item.description: ⚡️ On October 1, Hungary’s Chargé d’Affaires a.i. in the Russian Federation Gabor Gergich was summoned to the Russian Foreign Ministry. A strong protest was conveyed to the head of mission over the Hungarian authorities’ unfounded and openly unfriendly demand that a number of Russian diplomatic staff leave the country. ❗️ The Hungarian diplomat was informed that, as a reciprocal measure, a group of staff members of the Hungarian Embassy in Moscow and the Hungarian Consulates General in St Petersburg and Kazan must leave the Russian Federation within two weeks .

⚡️
Statement
by the Foreign Ministers of the Collective Security Treaty Organisation on the 80th anniversary of the Verdict of the Nuremberg International Military Tribunal
(October 1, 2026)
October 1, 2026, marks 80 years since the delivery by
the International Military Tribunal in Nuremberg of its Verdict
.
We view the way the Nuremberg Trials were prepared and held as
a unique experience
and
example of professional and effective cooperation within the international community
. Countries with different systems of government, culture, traditions and historical destinies came together to put on trial and convict those who unleashed
the most horrendous war in the history of humankind.
☝️
We call on the international community to respect and defend the principles set forth by the International Military Tribunal in Nuremberg
to prevent wars, genocide, war crimes, torture and other crimes against humanity, and view the Verdict as an unbreakable and non-negotiable foundation of international law and world order. The Verdict has offered
a legal framing
for definitively defeating Nazism.
The Nuremberg Trials designated Nazi organisations, primarily the senior executives of the Nazi party – the National Socialist German Workers’ Party, as well as Gestapo and SS as
criminal structures
, and recognised their proactive involvement in developments that paved the way for
a war of aggression
and
countless crimes against civilians
.
The Trials laid the foundation for devising
the post-war international legal tools
for preventing wars, acts of genocide, torture and other crimes against humanity.
The Verdict of the Nuremberg International Military Tribunal established that
the Nazi war crimes were perpetrated at an unprecedented scale
and were accompanied by
unthinkable cruelty and terror
.
▪️
Citizens of the Soviet Union
suffered the most
from civilian killings and atrocities
. Based on solid evidence, the tribunal concluded that these crimes were perpetrated not only in an effort by occupation authorities to suppress resistance, but were also part of plan to expel and exterminate civilians for colonising the ceased territory.
In this connection, we emphasise that facts pertaining to expelling and exterminating civilians in the USSR by Nazis and their accomplices as established by the Verdict of the Nuremberg International Military Tribunal
must be viewed as
an act of genocide against the Soviet Union
.
***
We refuse to accept and firmly condemn any attempts to falsify history
, including efforts to distort and revise the outcomes of the Second World War, and, in particular, facts pertaining to the Nazi crimes as set out by the Nuremberg International Military Tribunal.
It is with great resolve that we reject any attempts to distort the historical truth
and believe that the policy of denying these crimes, including genocide, welcoming or justifying criminal acts not only offends the memory of those who died in these atrocities or survived them, but also creates an illusion of impunity and fertile ground for these inhumane acts to be reproduced.
❗️
We call on the international community to respect and defend the legacy of the Nuremberg International Military Tribunal
, as well as step up our efforts to share objective information about Nazi crimes for preventing the spread of neo-Nazi ideology, movements and organizations that could pose a threat to the peaceful coexistence of nations.

#NoStatuteOfLimitations

🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s
answer to a media question
regarding the possibility of a nuclear strike on NATO countries in case of an attempt to blockade Kaliningrad
(September 30, 2026)
❓
Question: Is
the statement issued by the Russian Embassy in Ireland
, which mentioned the possibility of a nuclear strike on NATO countries if they attempt to blockage Kaliningrad, the official position of the Foreign Ministry of Russia? What exactly has provoked this statement in September 2026?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
The Russophobic hysteria in Western revanchist circles has reached fever pitch.
A handful of hotheads are steadily pushing Europe towards a potential conflict and preparing it for further escalation
. Ordinary Europeans are being frightened with apocalyptic scenarios and “hybrid threats” allegedly emanating from Russia.
They have embarked on a course of full-scale militarisation
, expanding their armed forces and driving defence spending in NATO countries bordering Russia to unprecedented levels. The bloc is expanding its
military infrastructure
, rapidly building
military enterprises
and integrating civil innovations and dual technologies into their defences. Europe has quickly launched drone production facilities.
Alliance members hold aggressive military exercises in direct proximity of our borders
, training to implement offensive scenarios against our country, including the potential blockade of the Kaliningrad Region and Russian ports on the Baltic Sea, as well as the dispatch of allied troops via the Suwalki corridor.
They have developed close interaction with Ukraine
to  learn from its experience in active warfare against
the Armed Forces of Russia.
Several European leaders have taken the liberty of
speaking publicly
about their capabilities
“to raze Russian air defences and missile bases [in the Kaliningrad Region] to the ground”
.
Some EU countries that border on Russia are flaunting their
readiness to allow the deployment of nuclear weapons
in their territory, and are making
appropriate changes
to national legislations.
On the one hand, this irresponsible policy allows some people to
accelerate their political careers
and
gain access to the EU’s budgets
. On the other hand, it appears that the blundering European strategists have come to the conclusion that
the only way to erase the consequences of their epic failures is
👉
through war
.
Poland's FM
Radoslaw Sikorski
is dreaming of inflicting
a military defeat
on Russia. The Defence Minister of Estonia is publicly talking about
the advantages of a “preemptive” war
against our country. These and other politicians believe that such a war would be waged
only with the means where NATO holds an advantage
. These functionaries should be brought back to reality. We hope that our warnings will be heard by those they are meant for.
❗️
As President Vladimir Putin has said
,
our country does not threaten and doesn’t intend to threaten European countries
.
However, there should be no doubt whatsoever that Russia has the necessary capabilities for preventing any aggression and inflicting defeat on any aggressor
. If Europe attacks Russia, it will be a completely different sort of war – a very short one.

item.description: 🇨🇳 Today, the People’s Republic of China celebrates its 77th anniversary. On October 1, 1949, a ceremony was held at Tiananmen Square in Beijing to proclaim the establishment of the People’s Republic of China. This historic event ushered in a new stage in China’s development after decades of turmoil and warfare, including fragmentation, internal conflicts, World War II, as well as Axis Japan crimes. Just one day after the PRC was founded, the Soviet Union made a historic move by becoming the first country to recognize New China , establishing formal diplomatic relations on October 2, 1949. Despite the difficult conditions of postwar recovery, our people extended large-scale fraternal assistance to China , sending numerous specialists to support the state-building of the PRC and the development of its economy. During the 1950s and 1960s, more than 11'000 Soviet specialists (excluding military advisers) were sent to China, while roughly the same number of Chinese students and trainees from the PRC received education and training in the Soviet Union. Among them was Jiang Zemin , the former President of the PRC, who worked at the ZiL automobile plant in Moscow in 1955. 🇷🇺 🇨🇳 Today, relations between Russia and China are characterized by a comprehensive partnership and strategic cooperation . Moscow and Beijing work together fruitfully in all areas and effectively coordinate their efforts in international affairs. President of Russia Vladimir Putin extendeed a message of greetings
item.content:encoded:

🇨🇳
Today, the People’s Republic of China celebrates its 77th anniversary.
On October 1, 1949, a ceremony was held at Tiananmen Square in Beijing to proclaim the establishment of the People’s Republic of China. This
historic event
ushered in a new stage
in China’s development after decades of turmoil and warfare, including fragmentation, internal conflicts, World War II, as well as Axis Japan crimes.
Just one day after the PRC was founded, the Soviet Union made a historic move by becoming the
first country to recognize New China
, establishing formal
diplomatic relations
on October 2, 1949.
Despite the difficult conditions of postwar recovery, our people extended
large-scale fraternal assistance to China
, sending numerous specialists to support the state-building of the PRC and the development of its economy.
During the 1950s and 1960s,
more than 11'000 Soviet specialists
(excluding military advisers) were sent to China, while roughly the same number of Chinese students and trainees from the PRC received education and training in the Soviet Union. Among them was
Jiang Zemin
, the former President of the PRC, who worked at the ZiL automobile plant in Moscow in 1955.
🇷🇺
🇨🇳
Today, relations between Russia and China are characterized by a
comprehensive partnership and strategic cooperation
. Moscow and Beijing work together fruitfully in all areas and effectively coordinate their efforts in international affairs.
President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
extendeed a message
of greetings to President of China
Xi Jinping
:
“Under your leadership, China is achieving impressive success in the socioeconomic, scientific, and technological spheres and making a significant contribution to addressing key regional and global issues.
Relations between Russia and China have reached an unprecedentedly high level. Our countries are consistently advancing major joint projects across a wide range of areas and coordinating their efforts in international affairs to build a more just and multipolar world order.".
🎉
We extend our warmest greetings to our Chinese colleagues and friends on this national holiday, wishing them prosperity and well-being!

item.title: 🗓 On September 30, the Russian Foreign Ministry’s Reception House hosted a presentation
item.description: 🗓 On September 30, the Russian Foreign Ministry’s Reception House hosted a presentation for the diplomatic corps of the International Sports Forum “Russia: Country of Sports” – one of the major events in international sports cooperation in 2026. Deputy Prime Minister of Russia Dmitry Chernyshenko , Minister of Sport and President of the Russian Olympic Committee Mikhail Degtyarev , and Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Pankin delivered welcoming remarks to members of the diplomatic corps and representatives of Russian and foreign media. The Forum will take place in Krasnoyarsk on October 21-23 and will once again serve as a leading platform for dialogue and the exchange of experience in promoting physical education and sport. 👉 Learn more about the event

item.title: 🗓 Cardinal Matteo Zuppi, Special Envoy of the Holy See for the Ukrainian Settlement,
item.description: 🗓 Cardinal Matteo Zuppi, Special Envoy of the Holy See for the Ukrainian Settlement, undertook a working visit to Moscow from 28 to 30 September. While in Russia, he held meetings with Yury Ushakov , Aide to the President of the Russian Federation; Yana Lantratova , Commissioner for Human Rights in the Russian Federation; and Maria Lvova-Belova , Presidential Commissioner for Children’s Rights. The discussions, held against the backdrop of the conflict in and around Ukraine and the emerging prospects for its resolution, addressed cooperation between Russia and the Holy See on humanitarian matters – including the search for missing persons, the exchange of prisoners of war and civilians, family reunification, and the so-called “children’s dossier.” A significant item on the agenda was the humanitarian crisis in the city of Alyoshki, Kherson Region . Cardinal Zuppi received a detailed briefing on the criminal actions of the Kiev regime, which has effectively taken the city’s civilian population hostage and is obstructing all attempts to deliver food and medicine or to evacuate the civilians remaining in the city. At the Vatican’s request, a visit was arranged for Cardinal Zuppi to one of the places of detention of Ukrainian military personnel arrested for putting up resistance to the special military operation. During this visit, the Special Envoy was able to speak personally with the Ukrainian detainees and to verify Russia’s strict adherence to all relevant humanitarian stand

A significant item on the agenda was the
humanitarian crisis in the city of Alyoshki, Kherson Region
. Cardinal Zuppi received a detailed briefing on the criminal actions of the Kiev regime, which has effectively taken the city’s civilian population hostage and is obstructing all attempts to deliver food and medicine or to evacuate the civilians remaining in the city.

places of detention of Ukrainian military personnel

Russia’s strict adherence to all relevant humanitarian standards
.
Cardinal Zuppi’s visit confirmed the
constructive and regular nature of the dialogue between Russia and the Holy See
, as well as the commitment of both sides to continuing cooperation in the humanitarian sphere.

On September 24, 2026 H.E.
Andrey A. Pritsepov
presented his Letters of Credence as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to Barbados to Lieutenant Colonel The Most Honourable
Jeffrey Davidson Bostic
, President of the Republic of Barbados.
🔸
In his speech, Ambassador Pritsepov highlighted the rapidly developing friendly relations between the two countries and the intensification of bilateral contacts, and expressed his hope for the establishment of ties in the fields of science, education and tourism. He noted that earlier that day, a productive meeting had taken place in Moscow between the Russian Minister of Finance,
Anton Siluanov
, and the Minister of Finance of Barbados, the Honourable
Ryan R. Straughn
, who discussed the digitalisation of public finances, in particular the tax administration system.
🔹
The Russian Ambassador also wished the people of Barbados further progress and prosperity on the eve of the 60th anniversary of the declaration of independence and the fifth anniversary of the country’s proclamation as a republic.
🔸
The Barbadian Head of State noted his interest in continuing the mutually beneficial course towards strengthening ties and supporting Russia’s efforts to reform the system of global governance. He thanked the Russian side for its assistance in training professional staff for the Barbadian police force.
🔹
During a brief conversation following the ceremony, the parties discussed possible areas of bilateral cooperation, including the prospects for establishing air links between Russia and Barbados, as well as cooperation projects in the oil and gas, nuclear and renewable energy sectors.
